headline: Business-travel momentum drives a beat-and-raise quarter
summary_short: Expedia reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4,315M (+14.0% y/y), led by 23% B2B growth, with GAAP net income of $878M (+166% y/y) and diluted EPS of $7.16 (+188% y/y); the company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $16.05-16.22B from $15.6-16.0B.
summary_long: Revenue grew 14% y/y, led by B2B (+23%), as Gross Bookings rose 12% and Booked Room Nights grew 6%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23% y/y (196bps margin expansion); GAAP operating income grew 65% y/y as revenue growth outpaced a 6.5% rise in total costs and expenses. Net income of $878M (+166% y/y) and diluted EPS of $7.16 (+188% y/y) were further lifted by a $293M favorable swing in other income (mainly gains on minority equity investments) and a 7.7% smaller diluted share count from buybacks. Expedia raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $16.05-16.22B (from $15.6-16.0B) and Gross Bookings guidance to $129.5-130.8B (from $127-129B).

drivers.explanation: CEO Ariane Gorin said Expedia exceeded the high end of its Q2 guidance, citing growth in consumer brands, sustained B2B momentum, and disciplined execution.
Revenue grew 14% y/y, driven by the B2B segment, which grew 23% y/y, per the release's own highlights.
Cost of revenue (ex-D&A) rose only 6.9% y/y ($377M to $403M) while revenue grew 14% y/y, expanding gross profit; a comparable Q1 2026 cost-of-revenue figure isn't broken out in the release.

Total costs and expenses grew only 6.5% y/y ($3,301M to $3,515M) while revenue grew 14% y/y, expanding operating income; the large q/q jump reflects Expedia's seasonally low Q1 versus peak Q2 travel demand.

Diluted EPS grew faster than net income, aided by a 7.7% smaller diluted share count (122.6M vs 132.8M shares y/y) from the $200M of buybacks disclosed this quarter.
